primitives.name: Binary Corroboration Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: # RB Lane — Verification Matrix (two-source rule) Slate: DraftKings NFL Week 2 main slate, Sun 2026-09-20 | Verified: 2026-09-19 (Sat, CDT) Rule: every material claim needs two independent sources or is flagged SINGLE/UNVERIFIED.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S': 'set of independent sources', 'M': 'material claim', 'V(S,M)': 'verification function over S and M'}
primitives.assumptions: Claims require V(S,M) = true for |S| ≥ 2; otherwise flagged.

layer2.mapping: GSI Bayesian update on M given evidence from S; GSE uses V(S,M) to filter valid state transitions.

primitives.name: Statistical Discrepancy Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Irving Week 1 line:** dknetwork recap 9/17 = 15 carries/81 yds/3 rec (vs BUF per prior notes) vs RotoWire Yahoo 9/18 = 8 carries/7 catches/93 yds/TD ("loss to Cincinnati").
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'X_i, X_j': 'statistical samples from sources i and j', '\\mu_i, \\mu_j': 'mean values of sample i and j', '\\sigma_i, \\sigma_j': 'standard deviations of sample i and j', '\\mathcal{D}': 'discrepancy distance function'}
primitives.assumptions: Discrepancies arise from labeling or measurement variance; must be resolved via meta-data alignment.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If \mathcal{D}(X_i, X_j) > threshold, flag as conflicting.

layer2.mapping: GSE uses \mathcal{D} to weight empirical estimates in state transition matrices; GSI applies \mathcal{D} to adjust posterior confidence bounds.

primitives.name: Projection Consistency Interval
primitives.verbatim_quote: **CMC Week 1 touches:** FantasyPros = 21 touches vs RotoWire Yahoo 9/18 = "just 15 touches." Discrepancy unexplained (possible receiving-touch counting difference).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\hat{\\theta}': 'estimated mean touches', 'z_{\\alpha/2}': 'critical z-score', '\\sigma': 'standard deviation of touch counts', 'n': 'sample size of observations'}
primitives.assumptions: Touch count data follows normal distribution; interval reflects sampling variability.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When \sigma is large or n is small, widen interval to [15, 21].

layer2.mapping: GSE constructs interval-based policy states; GSI computes interval overlap for cross-source agreement.

This dualism ensures minimal epistemic risk in high-stakes fantasy modeling. The statistical kernel for resolving discrepancies (e.g., Irving’s stats) operates under a distance metric that quantifies variance between datasets, enabling robust filtering of unreliable inputs. Projection intervals (e.g., CMC touches) are computed using standard error propagation, allowing GSI to model uncertainty ranges while GSE uses these for dynamic state transitions. These primitives form a closed-loop system where data integrity feeds into probabilistic reasoning and vice versa.
